body:
## 1. Why

Since 12 Oct, when ApplyPass moved from the Bubble app (v1) to this app (v2), Amplitude has lost where new users come from. Most v2 "New User" and "Page Viewed" rows show referrer and first UTM source as "(none); (none)".

Worked example: new users from Google search went from about 91 a week on v1 to 1 a week on v2. HubSpot, Reddit, ChatGPT and LinkedIn went to 0. Only the Google sign-in redirect and the `marketing_site` UTM survive. Nobody can read channel trends after 12 Oct from Amplitude.

## 2. What this changes

A visitor who clicks a Google ad and lands on `https://app.applypass.com/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc` now keeps that source in Amplitude through sign-in. A visitor sent by the marketing site (`www.applypass.com`) is now recorded as coming from `www.applypass.com`. Past events are not backfilled.

```text
BEFORE  landing /?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc  (referrer www.google.com)
        -> redirected to /sign-in            (UTM dropped by the redirect)
        -> Amplitude: referrer=www.google.com, utm_source = none
        -> after sign-in: utm_* unset, initial_referrer overwritten by the sign-in page
        Marketing site visitor: referrer = none (hidden by the SDK default)

AFTER   landing /?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc  (referrer www.google.com)
        -> redirected to /sign-in?utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=google
        -> Amplitude: initial_utm_source=google, initial_utm_medium=cpc,
                      initial_referring_domain=www.google.com
        -> after sign-in: no new campaign event, the properties stay
        Marketing site visitor: initial_referring_domain = www.applypass.com
```

## 3. Technical details

- **Problem**
  - The SDK's default `excludeReferrers` is `/applypass.com$/`. It skips `www.applypass.com`, so marketing-site visits show "(none)".
  - The return from Google sign-in or Stripe counts as a new campaign. The SDK then unsets `utm_*` and sets empty `initial_*` values.
  - `proxy.ts` redirects `/` to `/sign-in` without the query string, so UTM and click ids are gone before the SDK loads.
- **Fix**
  - `src/lib/analytics/amplitudeOptions.ts` (new): explicit `autocapture` object, since an object has to name `elementInteractions`, `frustrationInteractions`, `networkTracking` and `webVitals` to keep them on. `attribution.excludeReferrers` skips this app's own host and the Clerk and Stripe hosts only.
  - `src/lib/analytics/attributionParams.ts` (new) and `proxy.ts`: copy `utm_*` and ad click ids (`gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`, and others) onto the `/sign-in` and `/post-auth` redirects.
  - `docs/analytics-tracking-plan.md`: replaces the "no UTM captured" note.
  - `app/post-auth/page.tsx`: carries the same params through its `router.replace` to the final route, so a signed-in visitor keeps them past `/post-auth`.

Out of scope: backfill, dashboards, new tracking events.

## Proof

No visible change: app/post-auth/page.tsx only adds utm_* and click-id params to its router.replace target; the loading screen is unchanged.

- Red then green: `src/lib/analytics/attribution.test.ts` (4 tests, real SDK in jsdom on `app.applypass.com`), 2 tests in `proxy.test.ts`, and 3 tests in `app/post-auth/page.test.tsx` (params carried to `/dashboard`, next to a Settings return path, and to the `/plan-type` fallback). Related tests, lint, tsc and prettier pass.
- Local stack: app on `localhost:3100` with test Clerk and `api-test`, Chromium via Playwright, a `donotdelete` test account signed in with a Clerk ticket. Every `*.amplitude.com` request was answered locally, so no event reached any Amplitude project. The visitor arrived by clicking a link on a stand-in `http://www.google.com/` page, so `document.referrer` was real.

Captured `$identify` payloads, signed-out Google ad click (user properties only):

```text
BEFORE  land   $setOnce initial_referrer=http://www.google.com/  (no utm_*; URL was /sign-in with no query)
        sign-in $unset utm_*, ...   $set referrer=localhost:3100/dashboard (initial_* set again)
        return from accounts.google.com  $setOnce initial_referrer=http://accounts.google.com/, $unset utm_*

AFTER   land   $setOnce initial_utm_source=google, initial_utm_medium=cpc,
                        initial_referrer=http://www.google.com/, initial_referring_domain=www.google.com
               $set     utm_source=google, utm_medium=cpc, referrer=http://www.google.com/
        sign-in and the Google return: no further $identify
```

Marketing-site visitor (`http://www.applypass.com/` referrer, `/sign-up`): `initial_referring_domain=www.applypass.com` after the fix.

Limits of the local proof: on `localhost` the SDK default does not hide `www.applypass.com`, so the before/after for that case is covered by the jsdom test on `app.applypass.com`, not by the local run. The Google return is simulated as a page load with an `accounts.google.com` referrer, not a real Google sign-in. Screenshots (`before-A1-sign-in.png`, `after-A1-sign-in.png`) show the same sign-in page, since the fix changes data, not pixels.

## Intent

Make the v2 app send referrer and UTM properties to Amplitude like v1 did, shipped as a fix to dev.

Context from the funnel investigation (data/ff-232-amp-funnel/report.md in the firstmate home): since the 12 Oct move from the Bubble app (v1) to the v2 app, Amplitude loses the traffic source. Most v2 "New User" and "Page Viewed" rows show referrer and first UTM source as "(none); (none)".
- Worked example: Google search as a new-user source went from about 91 a week on v1 to 1 a week on v2; HubSpot, Reddit, ChatGPT and LinkedIn went to 0. Only the Google sign-in redirect and the marketing_site UTM survive. So channel trends after 12 Oct cannot be read from Amplitude.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change only touches analytics config and query strings. Checked against the installed SDK (2.45.7): autocapture flags behave the same as `autocapture: true` (performanceTracking is off in both), the exclude regexes match `referring_domain` (host with port, from referrer.split('/')[2]), and the post-auth carry covers the resolved route, the Settings return path, the /plan-type fallback, and the setPlanType re-resolve. The only finding is a small doc inaccuracy.

## Testing

- ⏭️ **Test** - skipped

<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 1 info</summary>

- ⚠️ `proxy.ts:46` - The signed-in branch now copies utm_*/click ids onto the /post-auth redirect. The commit message, the tracking-plan doc and the tests cover only the signed-out / -> /sign-in redirect, so this branch is untested and undocumented, and it likely loses the params anyway. Example: a signed-in user clicks app.applypass.com/?utm_source=hubspot -> 307 to /post-auth?utm_source=hubspot -> PostAuthContent resolves the route and calls router.replace('/dashboard') (app/post-auth/page.tsx:64). The Amplitude SDK starts only after the load event plus requestIdleCallback (up to 2s) plus a dynamic import of ./sdk (analytics.ts:226-235, runAfterPageLoad). CampaignParser reads location.search when init runs, so if the route resolves first, the SDK reads /dashboard and utm_* are lost. The referrer is still recorded. Decide whether returning signed-in visitors are in scope. If they are, carry the params through post-auth's router.replace (or read them before the replace) and add a test. If not, remove the copy at proxy.ts:46.

🔧 Fix applied.
1 info still open:

- ℹ️ `docs/analytics-tracking-plan.md:261` - Round 1's fix added a post-auth bullet to this doc but left the summary line behind. Line 261-262 says `attribution.test.ts` and `proxy.test.ts` "pin each one", but the post-auth carry (the third bullet, `app/post-auth/page.tsx`) is tested only in `app/post-auth/page.test.tsx`. A reader looking for the test that guards the signed-in path ends up in the wrong two files. Fix: add `app/post-auth/page.test.tsx` to the list of tests in that sentence.
